candidates: When registering a program in `ase/io/formats.py` that has both an input format and an output format, ensure each variant uses a distinct `magic` bytes value so ASE can reliably autodetect which type a given file is. Sharing the same magic string between input and output variants makes autodetection arbitrary.

In `FileIOCalculator` subclasses, set the class attribute `discard_results_on_any_change = True` directly on the class rather than overriding the `set()` method to achieve the same effect; the superclass recognises this attribute and handles it automatically.

Keep new `FileIOCalculator` subclass constructors minimal. Avoid forwarding parameters like `restart`, `ignore_bad_restart_file`, and `atoms` unless they are explicitly exercised by tests; these uncommon construction patterns are better served by dedicated factory functions.

When adding a new calculator, register its snake_case name in the `names` list in `ase/calculators/calculator.py` (so `get_calculator_class()` works and the test suite can monkeypatch and auto-skip it) and add its executable(s) to `default_executables` in `ase/calculators/autodetect.py` (so `ase info --calculators` reports it correctly).
New calculators should include an entry in `ase/test/standardization/test_ch4_energy.py` so they participate in the project-wide standardised multi-calculator energy benchmark.

Logic inside a calculator that depends only on external data (e.g., the command string, the job prefix, or a file path) should be extracted into standalone module-level functions rather than instance methods. This keeps the calculator class lean and makes the functions independently testable.

Use `round()` rather than `int()` when converting a floating-point value to an integer in ASE (e.g., summing initial magnetic moments). `int()` truncates toward zero and can produce wrong results due to floating-point rounding; `round()` gives the nearest integer as expected.

When using `subprocess.call` (or similar) in a context where the subprocess is intentionally expected to fail or exit non-zero (e.g., probing a launcher script with invalid input to extract a configuration value), add a comment explaining that failure is expected and describe what should happen if the command fails in an unexpected or silent way.

Do not manually create or enter a temporary directory inside individual tests (e.g., via `tmp_path` or `ase.utils.workdir`). The project's global `autouse=True` fixture in `conftest.py` already runs every test inside a fresh temporary directory; adding a redundant manual tmpdir setup is unnecessary.
